rescale.title: Rescale

info.intro: Rescaling adjusts the minimum and maximum values when rendering. In a single-band image the rescaled minimum maps to black and the maximum to white. Useful when you want to highlight features in a narrow value range (e.g. a DEM where you only care about 0–100m).
info.format: Format: {{format}}. Multiple rescale values can be supplied per band.
info.defaults: By default TiTiler rescales using the input datatype's min/max (e.g. 0–255 for 8-bit PNGs, 0–65535 for 16-bit). For DEMs and similar this can wash the image out - set explicit rescale values that make sense for your data.

rescale.help: Fixed min,max applied to each band.
rescale.helpPrefilled: Fixed min,max applied to each band. Pre-filled from known defaults for this collection.
rescale.noneHelp: No rescaling - raw pixel values are served as-is. Use a color formula or ensure your data range maps to 0-255 for display.

info.intro: Comma-separated tone-mapping operations applied in order. Each op is <name> <bands> <args>. Bands are any combination of R/G/B (e.g. RGB, RG, B).
info.gamma: gamma <bands> <value> - power-law correction. Values > 1 brighten midtones (darker → lighter); < 1 darken. Typical: 1.5–3.5.
info.saturation: saturation <value> - colour intensity. 1.0 = unchanged, > 1 more vivid, < 1 muted toward grayscale. Typical: 0.8–1.5. No bands arg.
info.sigmoidal: sigmoidal <bands> <contrast> <bias> - perceptual contrast curve. contrast 5–25 (higher = punchier); bias 0–1 (pivot point, 0.5 = center, > 0.5 lifts shadows).
info.commas: Commas between ops are required; the panel auto-inserts them on blur. <link>TiTiler docs</link>.

which.title: Which imagery to use
which.tooltip: Narrows which images from this catalog the campaign draws on. Advanced options add sort order, a custom CQL query, and the choice of pulling one single scene instead of a mosaic.
which.description: Pick the period to cover and how cloudy an image may be. Every image the campaign shows is searched for within these limits.

pull.title: What to pull from the catalog
pull.tooltip: A collection mosaic stitches every matching image in a time window into one seamless layer, and is what you want in almost every case. A single item pins the campaign to one specific scene.

catalog.startMonthTooltip: First month of the temporal range.
catalog.endMonthTooltip: Last month of the temporal range (inclusive).
catalog.itemSortTooltip: Controls the order in which STAC items are returned. For first-valid compositing, the first matching item wins - sorting by cloud cover puts the clearest images first.

groups.title: Mosaic groups and time periods
groups.tooltip: Groups are imagery collections, not the source STAC collection. Each group contains mosaics for smaller time periods, called slices.
groups.descriptionSingle: The whole date range forms one group (imagery collection). Choose the time periods for detailed imagery within it; each period becomes a mosaic slice.
groups.description: Organize mosaics into time-based groups (imagery collections), with detailed imagery periods (slices) inside each group. For example: monthly groups with weekly mosaics. These periods organize available scenes; they do not change how often the satellite captures new images.
groups.patternTooltip: Choose group and detailed imagery periods, or select Custom to set your own intervals.
groups.everyTooltip: Each group is an imagery collection. For example, 1 month creates one collection per month.
groups.sliceEveryTooltip: Each period becomes a mosaic slice within its group (collection). For example, 1 week creates weekly detailed imagery.
groups.summarySingle: One group (imagery collection) covers the full date range, with a detailed mosaic (slice) every {{slice}}.
groups.summary: Each group (imagery collection) spans {{window}}, with a detailed mosaic (slice) every {{slice}}.
